# Agent instructions

## Tooling

Use Bun for all repository operations.
Do not use `npm`, `npx`, or `bunx`.

- `bun test`: Run the full suite, including live E2E.
- `bun run test:live`: Run only live E2E.
- `bun run typecheck`: Run TypeScript type checking.
- `bun run lint`: Run `oxlint --type-aware .` with Ultracite core and anti-slop.
- `bun run format`: Apply Oxfmt formatting.
- `bun run check`: Check lint, formatting, types, and the full suite.
- `bun run build`: Build the ESM bundle to `dist/`.

Keep the Ultracite core and anti-slop lint rules unrelaxed.
Keep `ultracite`, `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` devDependencies on `latest`.
Keep Oxfmt `proseWrap: "preserve"`.

## OpenCode target

Target the latest available OpenCode V2 plugin API.
Keep `@opencode/core` and `@opencode/plugin` devDependencies on `latest`.
`^2.4.1` is the minimum `@opencode/plugin` peer floor, not a compatibility ceiling.
Keep `@opencode/plugin` and `effect` as runtime peers and external build imports.

## Code standards

- Import relative files with `.js` extensions (NodeNext resolution).
- Validate all plugin options in `parseConfig` (`src/config.ts`) with exact `Invalid plugin option <name>; expected <description>.` errors.
- Guard provider payloads with the JSON type guards in `src/types.ts`.
- Resolve credentials on every execution through `resolveCredential` (`src/auth.ts`).
- Never log, store, or include credential values in errors.
- Apply the shared cancellation and timeout pattern to every provider fetch.
- Return results that satisfy OpenCode's `WebSearch.Result` schema.
- Return `[]` when a valid response contains no grounded web sources.
- Limit `content` to model-generated text spans attributed to a source URL; never copy verbatim source excerpts.
- Read only provider `settings.baseURL` and fallback `settings.apiKey`; direct HTTP does not inherit the model pipeline.
- Preserve Google source URLs. `WebSearch.Result` cannot display `searchEntryPoint`; do not claim full Grounding Display Terms compliance.
- Google supports key credentials only; OpenCode has no built-in Google OAuth method. Keep the fail-closed rejection of non-key Google credentials.

## Test contracts

- Load `index.ts` through the latest `@opencode/core` in-process host (`tests/host.ts`) and the built-in `websearch` tool.
- Use no mocks: no loopback servers, provider payload fixtures, spies, global fetch patches, or imitated plugin contexts.
- Replace host layers only to isolate state (paths, config, watcher, location) and to skip permission prompts. Keep `Provider`, `Credential`, `WebSearch`, and `Tool` services unmodified.
- `websearch.test.ts` holds mock-free host contracts: registration and disposal, option validation through setup, fail-closed credentials, and pre-aborted signals.
- `tests/live.test.ts` holds live E2E against real OpenAI and Google APIs. `bun test` runs it by default.
- Read `openai` and `google` `settings.baseURL` and `settings.apiKey` read-only through OpenCode config resolution.
- Fail clearly on missing live prerequisites; do not skip. ChatGPT OAuth is not a live prerequisite.
- Never print live response bodies, gateway URLs, or credentials from live failures.
- Bound live prompts, cost, and request budgets. Set each test timeout above its plugin `timeoutMs`.
- Tests run concurrently (`bunfig.toml`). Give every host its own temporary directory and state; never mutate global user state or shared module state.
- Do not retain live provider responses as fixtures.

# opencode-websearch-addons

This OpenCode V2 plugin adds OpenAI and Gemini native web search providers to the built-in `websearch` tool.
It adds no custom tools.

It registers two providers:

- `openai`: OpenAI Web Search
- `google`: Gemini Google Search

The plugin requires `@opencode/plugin` 2.4.1 or newer.

## Installation

Add the package to your `opencode.json` or `opencode.jsonc` file.

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-websearch-addons",
    },
  ],
}
```

Register the package once; do not also load it from `.opencode/plugins/`.

Select a provider in the same file:

```jsonc
{
  "websearch": {
    "provider": "google",
  },
}
```

Both providers stay registered when you select one.
A missing credential causes an error only when its provider runs.

## Authentication

Connect the `openai` or `google` integration in OpenCode before you search.
The plugin reads the active connection on every search and stores no credentials.
When no connection is active, it uses the `apiKey` from the provider settings in your OpenCode configuration.

- OpenAI accepts API keys and ChatGPT OAuth connections.
- Google accepts API keys only, including keys from environment variables.

The plugin reads only two provider settings: `baseURL` and `apiKey`.
Other provider settings, such as custom headers, do not apply.
If you use a gateway, set `baseURL` to a gateway that supports native search.
OpenAI connections that use the `chatgpt-browser` or `chatgpt-headless` sign-in methods ignore `baseURL` and always use the ChatGPT endpoint.

## Options

Set options on the plugin entry:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-websearch-addons",
      "options": {
        "timeoutMs": 60000,
        "openai": { "reasoningEffort": "low" },
        "google": { "searchTimeRange": "lastMonth" },
      },
    },
  ],
}
```

| Option                     | Default                   | Allowed values                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `openai.model`             | `"gpt-6-luna"`            | Non-empty string up to 100 characters                               |
| `openai.reasoningEffort`   | `"medium"`                | `"none"`, `"minimal"`, `"low"`, or `"medium"`                       |
| `openai.searchContextSize` | `"medium"`                | `"low"`, `"medium"`, or `"high"`                                    |
| `openai.userLocation`      | none                      | Object with optional string `city`, `country`, `region`, `timezone` |
| `google.model`             | `"gemini-3.5-flash-lite"` | Non-empty string up to 100 characters                               |
| `google.thinkingLevel`     | `"medium"`                | `"minimal"`, `"low"`, or `"medium"`                                 |
| `google.searchTimeRange`   | `"any"`                   | `"any"`, `"lastDay"`, `"lastWeek"`, `"lastMonth"`, or `"lastYear"`  |
| `timeoutMs`                | `120000`                  | Integer from 100 through 120000                                     |

Set `openai.userLocation` only when you need location-biased results.

## Output

Each result has a source URL and can include a title, a publication time, and content.
The content is model-generated text that cites the source; it is not copied from the source page.
A search with no web sources returns no results.

Google can return `searchEntryPoint` search suggestions, but OpenCode has no place to display them.
For this reason, the plugin does not fully meet Google's [Grounding with Google Search terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms#grounding-with-google-search).
Review those terms before you use this plugin in a product.
The plugin keeps Google source URLs unchanged; do not rewrite them.

## Development

Use Bun 1.3 or newer for all scripts; the test suite uses concurrent test execution.

```sh
bun install
bun run check   # lint, format check, typecheck, and all tests
bun run build   # build dist/
```

Other scripts: `bun test`, `bun run test:live`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, and `bun run typecheck`.

`bun test` includes live searches against OpenAI and Google, which need network access and can incur charges.
Configure `settings.baseURL` and `settings.apiKey` for both `openai` and `google` in your global OpenCode configuration, or the live tests fail.
The live tests ignore project configuration.

# Changelog

All notable changes to `opencode-websearch-addons` are documented in this file.

## 1.1.1 (2026-11-24)

- Target OpenCode `v2.4.1`, raise the `@opencode/plugin` peer floor to `^2.4.1`, and keep Ultracite, Oxlint, and Oxfmt devDependencies on `latest`.
- Preserve the preceding generated passage when OpenAI `url_citation` offsets cover only a citation marker, prefer complete terminal SSE output, and handle headerless SSE responses.
- Update the test host for the flattened `websearch` tool output and the `Flag.Service` requirement in `@opencode/core` 2.4.1.
- Remove loopback servers, provider payload mocks, and spies from the test suite.
- Expand live E2E to cover default options, configured options, and an ungrounded prompt for both providers, and run test cases concurrently.
- Rewrite `README.md` as a short introduction, reduce `CONTEXT.md` to project decisions, and remove duplicated rules from `AGENTS.md`.

## 1.1.0 (2026-11-14)

- Move `@opencode/plugin` (`^2.3.0`) and `effect` (`^4.0.0`) to `peerDependencies`, externalize both in the distribution bundle, and remove legacy `ctx.catalog` compatibility shims.
- Route `chatgpt-token-sharing` OAuth credentials through the configured provider `baseURL` or `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses` without Codex headers, restrict the Codex endpoint to `chatgpt-browser` and `chatgpt-headless`, and reject unknown OAuth methods.
- Reject OpenAI `response.incomplete` stream events and JSON `status: "incomplete"` responses with redacted details, and send explicit `Accept: text/event-stream` headers.
- Accumulate Gemini `groundingChunks` and `groundingSupports` in arrival order across streamed events, deduplicate result URLs after support resolution, preserve source URLs unmodified, and reject `ESCALATION` and `PUP_LIMITED_DISABLED` finish reasons.
- Emit sanitized Effect `HttpClientError` causes on failed HTTP responses for host 429 cooldowns and status-specific messages, omit out-of-range publication timestamps (`±8.64e15` ms), and restrict result URLs to `http:` and `https:`.
- Narrow `openai.reasoningEffort` to `none`, `minimal`, `low`, and `medium`, narrow `google.thinkingLevel` to `minimal`, `low`, and `medium`, and privatize internal helpers and option constants.
- Replace helper micro-tests and fetch spies with an in-process `@opencode/core` host suite, loopback transport failure scenarios, and default live E2E tests reading configured OpenCode `baseURL` and `apiKey` settings.
- Migrate linting and formatting from vendored anti-slop rules to Ultracite, Oxfmt, and type-aware Oxlint (`oxlint --type-aware`), and reconcile `README.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, and `AGENTS.md`.

# Project decisions

## Target the latest OpenCode V2 release

Development uses `latest` for `@opencode/core` and `@opencode/plugin`.
The peer floor is `@opencode/plugin ^2.4.1` and `effect ^4.0.0`.
The bundle externalizes both peers so the plugin shares the host's runtime identity.

## Extend the built-in `websearch` tool

The plugin registers `openai` and `google` providers through `ctx.websearch`.
It adds no custom tools and does not change the selected provider.
Users keep one search tool and select a provider in standard OpenCode configuration.

## Use direct provider HTTP

Native search tools and citation data are not available through the plain text generation interface.
The plugin calls each provider's native search API directly.
It reads only `settings.baseURL` and fallback `settings.apiKey`.
It does not inherit headers, body overlays, or other model-pipeline settings, because merging them into search bodies is unsafe.

## Delegate credentials to OpenCode

OpenCode owns connections, stored credentials, OAuth renewal, and active selection.
The plugin resolves the active credential on every execution and keeps no credentials between executions.
OpenAI routes OAuth by `methodID`: `chatgpt-token-sharing` uses the key route, and `chatgpt-browser` and `chatgpt-headless` use the Codex route.
The plugin rejects unknown OAuth methods and external credentials.
Google accepts key credentials only, because OpenCode `v2.4.1` has no built-in Google OAuth method.
Revisit this decision if OpenCode adds one.

## Fail closed

Authenticated redirects, incomplete responses, and blocked responses are errors.
HTTP status failures become credential-free Effect `HttpClientError` values.
This keeps OpenCode 429 cooldowns and status-specific messages without exposing secrets.

## Attribute content and preserve sources

`content` holds only model-generated spans attributed to a source URL, never verbatim source excerpts.
Google source URLs stay unchanged, including redirect links.
`WebSearch.Result` cannot show Google `searchEntryPoint`, so the project does not claim full Grounding Display Terms compliance.

## Bound effort and thinking

The plugin limits OpenAI reasoning effort to `none` through `medium`.
It limits Google thinking level to `minimal` through `medium`.
Search requests stay fast and inexpensive.

## Test without mocks

Tests run the plugin in the real in-process OpenCode host.
Host contracts need no network, and live E2E calls the real OpenAI and Google APIs.
Mocks drift from upstream behavior, so the suite has no loopback servers, payload fixtures, or spies.
As a result, HTTP 429 cooldowns, redirect rejection, and error redaction rely on code invariants rather than automated tests.

## Keep tooling strict

Bun runs every script.
Type-aware Oxlint with unrelaxed Ultracite core and anti-slop rules, and Oxfmt, gate every change.
Keep `ultracite`, `oxlint`, `oxlint-tsgolint`, and `oxfmt` on `latest` instead of pinning versions.
